title: Quant Economics: Latency KPI-driven Quant Selector (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is an early working doc for a small, latency-KPI-driven quantization selector and micro-cost model. The goal: given a target p95 latency and a target per-token spend, recommend the least-aggressive quant format (INT8, FP8, 4-bit) that meets quality and latency constraints while minimizing unit cost.

Context + assumptions (high-level):
- We target production-style inference workloads (short-to-medium sequence, 32–512 tokens typical).
- Hardware profiles: H100 (80GB), A100 (40GB), and a smaller T4-like baseline for latency-sensitive edge cases.
- Quant formats supported: INT8 (per-layer symmetric/asymmetric), FP8 (E4M3/E5M2 variants), and 4-bit (GPTQ-ish schemes).
- Quality metric: relative perplexity increase (or task-specific accuracy drop) vs. FP16 baseline. We translate that to an allowable quality budget e.g., <= 2% absolute accuracy loss or <= 10% relative perplexity increase depending on workload.
- Cost model inputs: GPU $/hour effective (after infra overhead), concurrency and batching behavior, per-token compute time multipliers for each quant type.

Quick example spreadsheet snippet (columns in the eventual sheet):
Model | HW | Quant | Per-token latency (ms) | p95 latency (ms) | rel perf loss (%) | tokens/sec | cost_per_M_tokens ($)
m-13b | H100 | FP16 | 2.1 | 18 | 0.0 | 476 | 0.85
m-13b | H100 | INT8 | 1.6 | 14 | 1.8 | 625 | 0.62
m-13b | H100 | FP8  | 1.4 | 12 | 2.4 | 714 | 0.55
m-13b | H100 | 4-bit | 1.0 | 9  | 6.8 | 1000| 0.39
(These numbers are illustrative: get empirical profiling for each model/hw/seq-length combo)

Simple per-token cost derivation (sheet formula semantics):
- tokens_per_second = 1000 / per_token_latency_ms
- hourly_tokens = tokens_per_second * 3600 * concurrency_effective
- cost_per_M_tokens = (gpu_hourly_rate / hourly_tokens) * 1e6
Notes: concurrency_effective accounts for batching and pipeline utilization; for latency SLOs concurrency may be low.

Latency-first decision rule (greedy):
1) Given target_p95, filter out quant/hw rows where measured p95 > target_p95 * (1 + slack). Slack defaults to 0.05 (5%).
2) From remaining rows, filter by quality budget (rel perf loss <= allowed).
3) Pick row with minimum cost_per_M_tokens.
4) If no row passes both filters, consider fallback policies in order: increase hardware tier, increase batching (if SLO allows), or accept a higher-quality quant (e.g., FP8 -> INT8 -> 4-bit reversed).

Heuristic rules and knobs to bake into the tool: 
- tail-sensitivity multiplier: some workloads have heavy tail tokens (rare long outputs), p95 and p99 behave differently. Allow separate p-percentile targets.
- per-user SLO tiers: e.g., "interactive" (p95 <= 100ms), "nearline" (p95 <= 500ms).
- quality budget expressed either as absolute accuracy drop or as model-specific regression on a small eval set (recommended).
- penalize quant formats with higher variance in p95 across runs (add small cost margin).

Open experiments to run (priority):
- Microbench across seq lengths: 16, 64, 128, 256, 512 on A100/H100 for m-7b, m-13b, m-30b with all quant types. Collect mean, p50, p95, p99 latency and stddev.
- End-to-end task evals for representative workloads: search rerank, summarization, instruction-following. Measure task metric delta vs FP16.
- Batch scaling curves: measure how tokens/sec scales with batch sizes under latency constraints (simulate in-flight queue).

Quick worked example (customer scenario):
- Customer: chat product with target p95 <= 200ms, budget <= $1.00 per M tokens, allowed quality loss <= 3% rel perplexity.
- Profiling table snippet shows: on A100, INT8 p95 = 180ms cost = $0.72/M, FP8 p95 = 150ms cost = $0.60/M, 4-bit p95 = 120ms cost = $0.45/M but rel perf loss = 7%.
- Decision: FP8 on A100 meets p95 and quality budget and is cheapest of formats passing quality filter. Recommend FP8 with canary traffic at 5% and a small eval set run.

Recommendations for integration into Redwood Optimize product: 
- Add a small endpoint in the Cost Estimator that accepts: target_pXX, quality_budget, model_id, seq_profile, preferred_hw list. Returns ranked candidate quant/hw combos with estimated cost and confidence levels.
- Expose "safe defaults" per workload class (interactive/throughput/archival).
- Surface caveats: quant variability, model-specific sensitivity, and long-tail token behaviors.

Questions / unresolved: 
- How to map relative perplexity (model-agnostic) to human-visible task loss for customers? (Need per-workload calibration.)
- Should we include hybrid routing costs (i.e., route heavy tails to FP16 hardware dynamically)? Implementation complexity vs benefit?
- How to model multi-tenant noise on p95 for Dedicated pools (we need isolation factors from SRE).

TODOs (next steps):
- [ ] Run microbench experiments for m-13b on A100/H100 for the seq lengths above. (Owner: Marco)
- [ ] Build a small spreadsheet prototype with formulas and confidence bands. (Owner: Priya)
- [ ] Design API contract for Optimize to accept SLOs and return quant recommendations. (Owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Draft canary + rollback recipe for production rollout of recommended quant settings. (Owner: Jeremy)

Appendix: quick list of conservative knobs to reduce risk when recommending lower-precision: 
- Start at low traffic % (1–5%) with shadow checks comparing outputs (scalar metrics) to FP16 baseline.
- Evaluate on a seeded prompt set (50–200 examples) covering common failure modes.
- Track drift: auto-escalate to next safer quant level if quality regressions exceed threshold for >N min.

Notes to self: keep the UI flow simple: 3 inputs (pXX latency target, quality budget, cost target) -> single ranked table -> explainability bubbles (why recommended).

End of draft.

(Informal writing style: expect to iterate. This is intentionally not a polished playbook; it's a working requirements + example numbers doc to guide the prototype sheet and the first PR.)
